components: a looped right body with a descending tail
strokeOrder: start at the tip inside the small loop and curl clockwise round it
without lifting, go on round the bottom and up the outer left side
without lifting, arch over the top and come down to the bar
without lifting, carry the bar to the right
without lifting, go up the bar's right end and back over to the right loop
without lifting, go round the loop and down the tail — and only now lift
strokeOrderNote: one continuous stroke — six joined movements, no pen lift; order from Narale's four numbered parts, with the stroke count and direction from native writers' pen traces in HP Labs India's LipiTk Tamil recognizer, class 31, overriding the chart's four separate runs

strokeOrderSource.citation: Ratnakar Narale, Learn Tamil Through English/Hindi, Reading and Writing Tamil Granthakshars, Third Tamil Granthakshar ஷ, Sanskrit Hindi Research Institute, p. 13; drawn in one stroke after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 31 (ஷ): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native writers (MIT licence, 2012)
strokeOrderSource.variation: Narale's chart numbers ஷ's four parts in order: the inner loop, the outer left body, the joining bar and the right loop with its tail. This ductus used to draw them as four pen-down runs, but a numbered part of a teaching chart is not evidence of a lift. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 175 of the 188 stored prototypes of ஷ (93%) are one pen-down stroke. 170 of the 175 (97%) start at the upper left, inside the small loop, and 174 (99%) turn it clockwise; 126 (72%) turn the right loop clockwise too, and 174 (99%) end in the bottom fifth, at the foot of the tail. So this ductus overrides the four runs: it follows Narale's four parts in his order without lifting. The bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline spirals out of the inner loop into the outer body, and turns the bar's right end up and back left into the right loop, so the pen goes round the inner loop, on round the bottom and over the outer body into the bar, along the bar, up its right end and back over to the loop, round the loop and down the tail. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the stroke count, the start, the order and the direction, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline. The underlying HP Labs data is licensed for research use only, so only counts and shares are cited here, and no trace was copied. Tamil handwriting varies by school.

notes: Grantha-derived ṣa appears in borrowed words such as சந்தோஷம் (cantōṣam, happiness). Native writers draw it in one stroke: the curled left body, the bar, then the loop and its tail.
